title: Gaussian limit for correlated sign sums
statement: For a real correlation parameter $\rho\in[-1,1]$, let $\mu_n$ be the law on $\mathbb R^2$ of $n^{-1/2}$ times the sum of $n$ independent, identically distributed pairs of signs, where each pair has uniform first coordinate and its second coordinate is obtained by keeping the first with probability $(1+\rho)/2$ and otherwise reversing it. As $n\to\infty$, the probability measures $\mu_n$ converge weakly to the centered bivariate Gaussian law with unit marginal variances and correlation $\rho$.
